_doc: Ownership manifest for the mutation-authority campaign (plans 0042-0050). This is TOOLING/GOVERNANCE metadata, not sweepable game content, which is why it lives in tools/ and not data/. It is the SINGLE home for exact ownership facts: authority classes, protected fields, construction allowances, and temporary legacy writers. Code headers and systems docs point HERE; they must not copy these lists. Enforced by tools/validate_mutation_authority.gd, whose header documents the detected write forms and the known blind spots.
_schema_rules: ONE FIELD, ONE AGGREGATE. 'Class.field' may be claimed once across the whole manifest; a second claim fails E_DUPLICATE_CLAIM. The check spans sections, so owned_models and hosted_fields cannot split the same field between two aggregates.

owned_models = this aggregate owns the WHOLE model, and every mutable field it declares must appear in 'fields' or the gate fails E_UNCLASSIFIED_FIELD. Adding a field to such a model is therefore a manifest change too.

hosted_fields = fields this aggregate owns on a model SHARED with another aggregate. Registering ONE class under hosted_fields in TWO aggregates with DISJOINT field sets is legal and supported — it is how SealiftCohort splits troops (force: bn_ids) from hulls (sealift_fleet: hulls_by_type, cohort_state), and how GameStateData is shared. A hosted class need not be claimed exhaustively by any ONE aggregate, but its leftover fields are not free: see shared_model_policies below.

shared_model_policies CLOSES the hosted half. Every class appearing under any aggregate's hosted_fields must account for EVERY mutable field it declares: claimed by exactly one aggregate, or listed here with a 'classification' from the validator's closed vocabulary and a concrete 'why'. Unclassified fails E_UNCLASSIFIED_HOSTED_FIELD; claimed AND excluded fails E_CLAIMED_AND_EXCLUDED; an exclusion for a field that no longer exists fails E_DEAD_EXCLUSION. Without this a field added to GameStateData arrives unprotected and nothing says so.
This section is NOT a second ownership list. Claimed fields are DERIVED from hosted_fields, so repeating one here is an error, not a duplicate.

A classification that is a PROMISE — 'planned_transitional' and 'order_buffer' — must also name a 'plan'. The pointer has to sit under 'plan_dir' AND still resolve: a shipped plan is archived out of plan_dir, so the exclusion fails E_STALE_POLICY_PLAN exactly when its reason expires, while a pointer anywhere else could never go stale and fails E_SHARED_POLICY_SCHEMA. plan_dir is configured rather than hardcoded so the abstract fixture world proves the rule against its own directory instead of moving every time a real plan is archived.

The gate resolves the RECEIVER'S TYPE before judging a write, so protection only reaches fields on a TYPED object. Values inside an untyped Dictionary/Array are invisible (the validator header's aliased-container blind spot) — that is why a shared aggregate object is made a typed Resource before its fields are registered.

Field NAMES are what get protected, and an unresolvable receiver writing a protected NAME is reported as a backstop. Prefer distinctive names: 'cohort_state' rather than 'state', which is used all over this codebase for unrelated things.

construction_writers / legacy_writers list 'path' plus exact 'Class.field' symbols. An allowance that no longer writes anything fails E_STALE_ALLOWANCE, so removing the last write means removing the entry; legacy_writers additionally require a removal_plan.

shared_model_policies._doc: The turn's whole value object. Five aggregates already claim a slice of it, so its remaining fields are where an unprotected field would hide most easily — hence the exhaustive list below. Most of it is either a request queue players fill, a report a phase emits, or state a named campaign plan is about to take ownership of.

turn_length_days.why: Scenario cadence copied onto the state by GameState.reset from GameData.turn_length_days (and floored to 1 there). No phase writes it during a game.

last_mobilization_summary.why: The mobilization phase's report for the turn just resolved: replaced wholesale by the phase that produced it, cleared at reset, and read only by serialization/observation (TurnEventLog / TurnResult). Not an evolving quantity, so there is no transition to protect.

last_air_insertion_summary.why: The air-insertion phase's report for the turn just resolved: replaced wholesale by the phase that produced it, cleared at reset, and read only by serialization/observation (TurnEventLog / TurnResult). Not an evolving quantity, so there is no transition to protect.

isolated_air_landed_brigades.why: Recomputed wholesale every turn by TurnConductor from ReinforcementPhases.isolated_air_landed_brigades(state). Supply isolation is DERIVED from corridor reachability, never asserted onto this field.

not_ashore_by_type.why: A cache of PendingBattalions.by_brigade_and_type over the three off-map pools. GameStateData.refresh_not_ashore_by_type() is its only writer and recomputes it from those pools, which are themselves protected (ship_reserve, mainland_pool, AirInsertionState.pool).

last_contested_hexes.why: The contest-detection phase's record for the turn just resolved, replaced wholesale by the phase that produced it. NOT write-only, and not merely serialized either: TurnConductor.gd:84 and :269 drive the ground-combat and FEBA-retreat loops straight off it, so a LATER phase depends on it. It stays unprotected because the authoritative state it describes lives elsewhere and this is a report of it — but renaming or reshaping it is a behaviour change, not a doc edit.

last_combat_summaries.why: The ground-combat phase's report for the turn just resolved: replaced wholesale by the phase that produced it, cleared at reset, and read only by serialization/observation (TurnEventLog / TurnResult). Not an evolving quantity, so there is no transition to protect.

last_ijfs_summary.why: The IJFS phase's record for the turn just resolved, replaced wholesale by the phase that produced it. NOT write-only, and not merely serialized either: the air-insertion phase feeds it to AirInsertionResolver.threat_from_ijfs_summary (ReinforcementPhases.gd:270), so a LATER phase depends on it. It stays unprotected because the authoritative state it describes lives elsewhere and this is a report of it — but renaming or reshaping it is a behaviour change, not a doc edit.

last_ijfs_writeback.why: The IJFS writeback phase's record for the turn just resolved, replaced wholesale by the phase that produced it. NOT write-only, and not merely serialized either: the maneuver-casualty step takes its casualties (FiresPhases.gd:60) and the anti-ship step hands it to AntishipTransitions.apply_ijfs_effects (FiresPhases.gd:78), so a LATER phase depends on it. It stays unprotected because the authoritative state it describes lives elsewhere and this is a report of it — but renaming or reshaping it is a behaviour change, not a doc edit.

last_antiship_summary.why: The anti-ship phase's record for the turn just resolved. Replaced wholesale by the phase that produced it, which then reads it straight back in the SAME function to stamp wave_bns onto it, emit it and return it (FiresPhases.gd:140-143) — so it is not a cross-phase handoff, but it is not write-only either. It stays unprotected because the authoritative state it describes lives elsewhere and this is a report of it.

last_offload_summary.why: The offload phase's report for the turn just resolved: replaced wholesale by the phase that produced it, cleared at reset, and read only by serialization/observation (TurnEventLog / TurnResult). Not an evolving quantity, so there is no transition to protect.

last_sealift_sent_by_type.why: The sealift send phase's record for the turn just resolved, replaced wholesale by the phase that produced it. NOT write-only, and not merely serialized either: the anti-ship crossing reads it as the crossing manifest (FiresPhases.gd:98), so a LATER phase depends on it. It stays unprotected because the authoritative state it describes lives elsewhere and this is a report of it — but renaming or reshaping it is a behaviour change, not a doc edit. Here that elsewhere is SealiftState.cohorts, which the sealift_fleet and force aggregates already protect.

last_frontline_summary.why: The front-line phase's record for the turn just resolved. Replaced wholesale by the phase that produced it, which then reads it straight back in the SAME function to replay its moves through GameData.set_brigade_hex (FrontlinePhase.gd:18-21) — so it is not a cross-phase handoff, but it is not write-only either. It stays unprotected because the authoritative state it describes lives elsewhere and this is a report of it.

last_cleanup_summary.why: The cleanup phase's record for the turn just resolved. Replaced wholesale by the phase that produced it, which then reads it straight back in the SAME function to latch game_over and winner off it (TurnClosure.gd:55-58) — so it is not a cross-phase handoff, but it is not write-only either. It stays unprotected because the authoritative state it describes lives elsewhere and this is a report of it.

shared_model_policies._doc: The force aggregate protects a brigade's runtime facts. What is left is OOB identity fixed at construction — and deliberately left unprotected, because a protected field NAME is claimed repo-wide: registering `id` or `name` would turn every unrelated `.id =` in the tree into an unresolved-write failure, which is exactly what IjfsMunition.name cost plan 0046 (22 innocent view-layer lines).

id.why: OOB brigade id, written only by GameData._load_oob_file(). Registering the NAME 'id' would flag unrelated `.id =` writes repo-wide.

name.why: OOB brigade name, written only by GameData._load_oob_file(). `name` is also a built-in Node property, so registering it poisons every scene-building line in the tree.

team.why: Which side the brigade belongs to, fixed by the OOB file at load.

to_number.why: Theater of operations the brigade belongs to, fixed by the OOB file at load.

nato_type.why: NATO unit-type symbol from the OOB, used for display and strength lookup; fixed at load.

shared_model_policies._doc: The force aggregate protects surviving quantity. The other two members are the battalion's type and a computed property over it.

type.why: Battalion type string from the OOB, written only by GameData._load_oob_file() and used to look up strength. Fixed for the life of the object.

combat_strength.why: Not storage: a getter-only computed property returning UnitStats.strength_for_type(type, 1.0) * qty. It has no setter and no backing field; the validator's member-declaration scan sees the `var name: Type:` form, so it must be classified even though nothing can write it.

shared_model_policies._doc: The force aggregate protects the pool and the landed list (plan 0044). The lift capacity and the insertion ledger on the same object are plan 0048's AirInsertionTransitions.

first_turn.why: Earliest turn air insertion may run, read from the scenario by AirInsertionStateBuilder.build() and never written again.

shared_model_policies._doc: The ijfs aggregate claims the three containers that persist across days. The rest splits exactly as the model's own header does: content loaded once by IjfsStateBuilder, and per-run ledgers reset at the top of every run_daily.

aggregates.summary: The Green anti-ship establishment: surviving launchers, permanent losses (IJFS and launch attrition), and temporary suppression, held as AntishipSystem rows plus the container-level projection the IJFS targets.

owned_models._doc: Owned model: EVERY mutable field must be classified below or the gate fails. Lifetimes: identity = fixed at construction; establishment = original strength; campaign = persists across turns; transient = reset each turn/crossing.

hosted_fields._doc: Fields this aggregate owns on a model SHARED with other aggregates. Only the listed fields are protected; GameStateData's remaining fields are claimed by plans 0044-0049.

construction_writers.why: load_systems() initialises FRESH, unpublished AntishipSystem rows from the grouping spec before anything holds them. It never accepts live establishment state.

aggregates.summary: The force aggregate migration: brigade roster, runtime placement/activity, placement-index writes, air-insertion pool/landed, and mobilization pending/released are routed through ForceTransitions. Caps/history on AirInsertionState are companion updates by ReinforcementPhases and are NOT registered here.

owned_models._doc: Plan 0044 slice: pending and released are force aggregate fields (drained/appended by ForceTransitions).

hosted_fields._doc: Plan 0044 slice: pool and landed are force aggregate fields (drained/updated by ForceTransitions). caps, history, initial_caps, first_turn are companion/identity fields excluded from this aggregate.

Plan 0044 SEA-TRANSPORT remainder: ship_reserve troop membership (BN ids in entries) is protected. JLSF cargo pseudo-entries (cargo='jlsf') are companion and exempt from force validation. Plan 0048 added the MobilizationState handle: this aggregate already owns every field of that model, so the handle lives with its contents rather than in an authority of its own — the same reasoning that puts infrastructure_state with the node fields.

Plan 0044 SEA-TRANSPORT remainder: mainland_pool and the cohorts array (which cohorts exist) are force aggregate fields, drained/appended by ForceTransitions. The hull queues on the same model — return_pipeline, escort_sam, escort_sam_max, escort_sam_threshold, escort_reload — are claimed by the sealift_fleet aggregate (plan 0045).
Runtime placement index projection; construction and reset also route through ForceTransitions so the host file has no writer exemption.
Runtime force fields protected during plan 0044. Identity/OOB fields remain construction-only source data and are not registered to avoid generic id/name false positives.
Force authority protects surviving battalion quantities; type is identity loaded from OOB data.

Plan 0045 typed cohorts: who is ABOARD one in-transit ship group. The hulls in the same cohort (hulls_by_type) and the leg it is on (cohort_state) belong to the sealift_fleet aggregate — one object, two authorities, split by field.

construction_writers.why: load_brigades()/load_scenario() construct fresh Brigade resources and initial placement facts from OOB/scenario data before runtime play mutates them.
build() constructs a FRESH AirInsertionState from scenario data before any runtime play mutates it.
build() constructs a FRESH MobilizationState from scenario data before any runtime play mutates it.
build() constructs a FRESH SealiftState from scenario data before any runtime play mutates it.
The sent()/offloading() factories fill a FRESH cohort from a caller's plan before it is appended to any SealiftState. A cohort in flight is never rewritten here.

aggregates.summary: The hull side of the amphibious lift (plan 0045): the ShipState fleet projection (which bucket every surviving hull of a type is in), the persistent hull queues SealiftState holds, the sealift_state handle, and the crossing's BN-equivalent loss ledger (plan 0050). Its counterpart is the 'force' aggregate, which owns who is ABOARD a cohort; this one owns what FLOATS and what sank. A cohort is shared by field, never reached across.

owned_models._doc: Owned model: EVERY mutable field must be classified below or the gate fails. ShipState is wholly a fleet projection, so no other aggregate has a claim on any of its fields. Lifetimes: identity = fixed at construction; establishment = the hulls the scenario starts with; campaign = persists across turns; projection = recomputed from SealiftState on every fleet write.

hosted_fields._doc: The fleet dictionary (ship name -> ShipState), the SealiftState handle itself, and the crossing's BN-equivalent ledger (plan 0050). Replacing the fleet or the handle is a scenario reset, which routes through SealiftTransitions.rebuild_fleet / install_campaign_state so the host file earns no writer exemption. The ledger pair is here rather than with the anti-ship launchers because it is the BN-equivalent conversion of the HULL losses this aggregate books: pending_lost_at_sea is whole BNs awaiting the offload phase's report, lost_at_sea_accumulator the same conversion's fractional remainder. pending_lost_at_sea is `campaign`, not `transient`: it survives a turn in which no wave crosses.

The hull queues on the model the force aggregate shares (plan 0045). mainland_pool and cohorts are the force aggregate's troop-side fields and are claimed there; these five are the hull side. The hull counts INSIDE a cohort are not a field of their own — they live in untyped cohort dictionaries the scanner cannot see into, which is what plan 0045's typed-cohort step exists to fix.

Plan 0045 typed cohorts: what FLOATS in one in-transit ship group and which leg it is on. bn_ids on the same model is the force aggregate's. cohort_state is spelled out rather than 'state' because the gate protects field NAMES and 'state' is used everywhere else in this codebase for something unrelated.

construction_writers.why: The sent()/offloading() factories fill a FRESH cohort from a caller's plan before it is appended to any SealiftState. Hull counts of a cohort in flight are only ever changed by SealiftTransitions.

build() seeds each escort type's SAM magazine at its scenario loadout while assembling a FRESH SealiftState, before anything holds it. The magazine is left empty when the scenario does not model reload.

build() constructs a FRESH ShipState per ship definition, all hulls ready, before anything holds the fleet. It never accepts live fleet state; replacing a LIVE fleet goes through SealiftTransitions.rebuild_fleet.

aggregates.summary: Persistent IJFS campaign state: the target list and every target's lifecycle (detection, posture, intel lock, suppression, destruction, MANPADS stock), Red munition magazines, Red squadron strength, and the day-to-day continuity of all three.

owned_models._doc: Owned model: EVERY mutable field must be classified below or the gate fails. manpads_remaining is the typed MANPADS stock plan 0046 lifted out of `metadata`; the metadata key of the same name is a serialization mirror the authority keeps in step, because metadata is aliased live into the ledger rows.
Owned model. Only inventory_remaining moves at runtime; the rest is content.

Owned model. losses_today is CAMPAIGN-cumulative despite its name — nothing resets it, and it is serialized into the air_oob_after ledger. rtb_today has no runtime writer at all and must not gain one; both are pinned by tests/ijfs/ijfs_authority_characterization_test.gd.

hosted_fields._doc: The three containers that persist across days (IjfsDailyState.gd's own header says so). The per-run ledgers and AD-health snapshots on the same object are rewritten wholesale by every run_daily and are outputs, not campaign state, so they are deliberately unregistered.
The IJFS handles GameStateData hosts. last_ijfs_summary / last_ijfs_writeback are phase OUTPUTS and stay unregistered, like every other phase summary.

construction_writers.why: Builds FRESH target/munition/squadron rows from the content files before anything holds them, and enriches SAM scores on rows still inside IjfsStateBuilder.build. It never accepts live campaign state.
Assembles the IjfsDailyState containers inside build(); nothing holds the state until it returns.

aggregates.summary: The port/airbridge lifecycle (plan 0047): each node's seizure/repair status, its repair clock, and its JLSF deployment marker, plus the node container and the InfrastructureState handle GameStateData holds. Ownership of the HEX a node sits on belongs to the 'map' aggregate; this one never writes a hex, and the map authority never writes a node.

owned_models._doc: Owned model: EVERY mutable field must be classified below or the gate fails. The field is node_status rather than status because a protected field NAME is claimed repo-wide and 'status' is used all over this codebase for unrelated things; the SERIALIZED key stays "status". Lifetimes: campaign = persists across turns.

Owned model, and it owns exactly one mutable field: the infra_id -> InfrastructureNodeState mapping. The per-node fields are the owned model above; typing them is what made either protectable at all, since values inside an untyped Dictionary are invisible to the gate.

hosted_fields._doc: The InfrastructureState handle itself. Replacing it is a scenario reset, which routes through InfrastructureTransitions.rebuild_infrastructure so the host file earns no writer exemption. jlsf_orders on the same model is an ORDER BUFFER, not node state, and stays unregistered like every other order array.

construction_writers.why: build() fills a FRESH InfrastructureState with one node per definition before anything holds it. It never accepts live node state; replacing a LIVE map goes through InfrastructureTransitions.rebuild_infrastructure.

aggregates.summary: Per-hex runtime state (plan 0047): who holds each hex and where the front line sits inside it, plus the hex_states container itself. Hex definitions, geometry and terrain are immutable content and are NOT part of this aggregate. Ownership is DERIVED from brigade occupancy by HexOwnershipCalculator and applied here; the authority offers no way to assert an owner, which is what makes the sticky-ownership invariant unbreakable rather than merely documented.

owned_models._doc: Owned model: EVERY mutable field must be classified below or the gate fails. The field is hex_owner rather than owner because a protected field NAME is claimed repo-wide and `owner` is a built-in Node property, so a future scene-building line would fail this gate falsely; the SERIALIZED key stays "owner" and is live in every game record's final_snapshot. Lifetimes: campaign = persists across turns.

hosted_fields._doc: The hex_id -> HexState container. brigades_by_hex on the same model is the force aggregate's placement index and is claimed there; the two are disjoint by field. Construction and reset route through MapTransitions as well, so the host file has no writer exemption and this aggregate needs no construction allowance at all.

aggregates.summary: The PLAAF air path's LIFT (plan 0048): the per-lift-class battalions-per-turn budget, the budget it started with, the append-only insertion log, and the AirInsertionState handle GameStateData holds. Who is in the pool and who has landed belongs to the 'force' aggregate (plan 0044) — one model, two authorities, split by disjoint fields, exactly as SealiftCohort splits troops from hulls. This authority never moves a battalion, and the force authority never touches a cap. Cap erosion is DERIVED from the resolver's packet rows rather than assigned, so a raised cap is not merely refused, it is unexpressible.

hosted_fields._doc: The lift half of the model: what a class can still fly, what it could fly at H-hour, and the log of every packet. pool and landed on the same model are the force aggregate's. first_turn is scenario identity written once at build and is excluded under shared_model_policies rather than claimed — it participates in no invariant this authority enforces. Lifetimes: campaign = persists across turns.

The AirInsertionState handle itself. Replacing it is a scenario reset, which routes through AirInsertionTransitions.rebuild_air_insertion_state, so the host file earns no writer exemption. air_insert_orders on the same model is an ORDER BUFFER, not lift state, and belongs to plan 0049.

construction_writers.why: build() sets the initial lift budgets on a FRESH AirInsertionState from scenario data before anything holds it. Replacing a LIVE state goes through AirInsertionTransitions.rebuild_air_insertion_state, which calls this builder rather than accepting a caller-built state.

aggregates.summary: The Red theater DOS balance and its audit ledger (plan 0049): current_dos_tons is the authoritative pool, day_history is the append-only row per billed day, and the SupplyState handle GameStateData holds. SupplyBill (scripts/calc/) decides who eats; this authority alone spends the pool. The new balance is DERIVED from the consumption row rather than accepted, so a row that disagrees with the pool is unexpressible and no second running total exists to drift.

owned_models._doc: Owned model: EVERY mutable field must be classified below or the gate fails. Lifetimes: campaign = persists across turns. Both fields are campaign state — the pool survives every turn boundary (a turn that restored it would make the whole DOS mechanic inert) and the ledger is append-only for the life of the game.

hosted_fields._doc: The SupplyState handle itself. Replacing it is a scenario reset, which routes through SupplyTransitions.rebuild_supply_state (reached from GameState via TurnClosure, the supply phase's owner), so the host file earns no writer exemption.

construction_writers.why: build() fills a FRESH, unpublished SupplyState with the scenario's starting pool before anything holds it. Replacing a LIVE state goes through SupplyTransitions.rebuild_supply_state, which is the only caller.

aggregates.summary: The four request queues players fill during planning and the turn drains during resolution (plan 0049): move orders, commitments, air-insert orders and JLSF deployments. They are one aggregate because the questions worth asking are about the SET — is anything accepted outside PLANNING, does anything survive begin-next-turn — and an answer split across four authorities is not an answer. OrderValidator (scripts/calc/) decides legality and appends nothing; OrderTransitions asks it and appends only on accept, so a rejection cannot half-apply.

hosted_fields._doc: The four order queues. `orders` and `commitments` are Team -> Array request maps cleared at begin-next-turn; `air_insert_orders` and `jlsf_orders` are consumed mid-resolution by the phase that acts on them, which is why the authority separates clear_turn_buffers from the two consume_* operations. Lifetimes: transient = reset each turn.

aggregates.summary: Where the game IS (plan 0049): the turn counter, the phase, and the three victory latches the end-of-turn census sets together. TurnLifecycleTransitions offers the three legal EDGES of the cycle (PLANNING -> RESOLUTION -> END -> PLANNING) and no destination setter, so an arbitrary phase assignment is unexpressible and a wrong-source call is refused without mutating anything. The counter moves on exactly one edge. The latch trio is applied from ONE CleanupSummary and the landing latch is derived from its census with `or`, so it cannot be disarmed short of a scenario reset. This authority decides no phase ORDER — TurnConductor still holds the ordered list — calls no other authority, and consumes no dice.

hosted_fields._doc: Turn/phase lifecycle plus the victory latches. Lifetimes: campaign = persists across turns (the latches and the counter both survive every turn boundary and are cleared only by a scenario reset); phase is campaign for the same reason — it is never reset per turn, it is ADVANCED.
